interfaces.name: Web application
interfaces.classification_rationale: Actions are expressed by manipulating presented affordances (content calendar, composer, approval queues, social inbox, analytics views) of a persistent, navigable representation of workspace state. Affordance Manipulation.

provenance.evidence: Provider product page describes the web workspace: create, plan, collaborate, approve, schedule, analyze, and a social inbox, navigated as views and controls.
Provider-hosted web application entry point (login/register), confirming a first-party browser client.

interfaces.name: Mobile application
interfaces.classification_rationale: First-party mobile client that presents the same affordance-driven navigable representation (calendar, feed, grid, previews, approvals) on the mobile surface. Separate Interactive interface from the web client per the surface checklist.

provenance.evidence: Provider (Planable Inc.) Google Play listing: create, schedule, preview, and approve content; calendar/list/feed views on mobile.
Provider App Store listing linked from planable.io, confirming a first-party iOS client.

interfaces.name: Public API
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes provider-defined REST operations (workspaces, pages, posts, media, labels, stories) via structured HTTP requests with Bearer-token auth and an OpenAPI 3.1 spec. Operation Invocation.

provenance.evidence: Provider guide: versioned REST API under /api/v1, Bearer token auth, OpenAPI 3.1 at /api/v1/openapi.json; explicitly states webhooks are not available in v1 (poll instead).
Provider help article describing token generation, scopes, and programmatic read/write access without logging into the app.

interfaces.name: MCP connector
interfaces.classification_rationale: Exposes semantically described Planable capabilities (create/update drafts, review approval queues, pull analytics, audit calendars, approve posts) that MCP-compatible AI tools discover and select as part of the interaction contract. Capability Discovery and Invocation, so Agentic rather than Programmatic despite tools ultimately being invoked.

provenance.evidence: Provider help article: single MCP server URL (mcp.planable.io/mcp) that any MCP-compatible AI tool connects to and authorizes to interact with Planable content.
Provider guide describes the connector giving compatible AI tools authorized access to act on real account data across the content workflow via MCP capabilities.

access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Embedded AI generation feature invoked via UI affordances (Generate with AI, Answer with AI) inside the web/mobile composer and social inbox; folds into those Interactive interfaces, not a separate consumer-facing interface.

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: Public API interactive docs / OpenAPI console (api.planable.io/api/v1/docs)
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: API explorer and documentation surface that issues the same REST operations; part of the Public API Programmatic interface, not a distinct navigable representation of service state.

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: Zapier connector and Zapier Integration API (app.planable.io/api/integrations/zapier), including its webhooks
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Third-party integration; the provider-hosted API and its webhooks exist solely to power the Zapier connector (OAuth app pairing) and are not offered as a general-purpose provider interface. The general-purpose Public API has no webhooks in v1.
No first-party desktop application found; only third-party Android emulators (e.g., BlueStacks) run the mobile app on PC/Mac.
No provider command-line tool or terminal dashboard found in official documentation.
None offered as distinct interfaces; the OpenAPI spec imports into third-party API clients (Postman/Insomnia), which are not provider interfaces.

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: Outbound social-network integrations (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, X, Threads, Google Business Profile)
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: These are Planable publishing outward to social platforms, not access mechanisms into Planable.
Third-party integrations, not provider-defined access interfaces.
